Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Quick recap + next steps (unit economics)

Thanks again for the call earlier, Samir and Elena — good discussion and nice to meet the team. TL;DR of the outcomes and asks: 

- Goal: pilot Redwood to power three LLM features in your lending product (smart summaries in underwriting, automated document ingestion + QA, and eligibility suggestion).
- You indicated ~150k MAUs initially, with an estimate of ~200 tokens/request for summaries and ~1k tokens/request for ingestion QA.
- You asked for target pricing guidance and an example unit-econ model to evaluate margin impact and CAC payback.

Could you confirm the ballpark monthly token volumes (ranges are fine) and the procurement timeline? Specifically: 
1) Expected monthly requests for each feature (or overall requests).
2) Typical tokens per request (you mentioned 200 / 1k — confirm).
3) Target price range for evaluation (e.g., $/1M tokens target, or monthly budget band).

I attached a simple worksheet that shows how we model $/feature given $/1M tokens and different batching/quant profiles. Based on the numbers you shared on the call, I sketched a conservative model — we can refine once you confirm volumes.

Next steps I propose:
- You: confirm the three items above and procurement window.
- Me: update worksheet + send a 30/60/90 pilot proposal with pricing bands (I’ll include recommended token-optimization knobs and expected unit costs).

Attachments: Redwood-Unit-Econ-Worksheet.xlsx (sketch), Proposed-Pricing-Grid.pdf (example bands)

Thanks — talk soon.
—

Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps (unit economics)

Marissa — thanks for the recap and for the worksheet. Quick answers below: 

1) Volumes (initial pilot month / steady state target):
   - Smart summaries: 50k requests month 1 -> 250k steady state
   - Doc ingestion + QA: 10k requests month 1 -> 60k steady state
   - Eligibility suggestion (low-latency microservice): 200k requests month 1 -> 800k steady state

2) Tokens per request:
   - Summaries: ~200 tokens avg (output-heavy)
   - Ingestion/QA: ~1,000 tokens (longer docs)
   - Eligibility suggestion: ~40 tokens (short prompt + small completion)

3) Target price / budget:
   - Procurement expects to see unit pricing that lands total monthly spend for steady-state in the $25k–$60k range depending on optimizations.
   - For evaluation, they want an example band for $/1M tokens so they can model outcomes — they mentioned wanting to target ~$40–$80 / 1M tokens as a starting internal benchmark.

Notes: Finance will run the formal procurement in 6–8 weeks; security/compliance will want SOC2 evidence (we can share your docs). We’re also going to evaluate end-to-end latency for the eligibility suggestion (sub-100ms target).

Happy to hop on another short call if that helps — otherwise send your updated worksheet and pilot proposal.

—
Samir Khan
Head of Product — FintechX
samir@fintechx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@fintechx.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@fintechx.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-09T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps (unit economics)

Samir — perfect, thanks for the specifics. I updated the worksheet and attached a pricing grid with 3 bands: Pilot, Growth, Steady-state. High-level observations and an example unit-econ mapping below (see attachments for the workbook calculations):

Example steady-state token mix (using your steady-state volumes):
- Summaries: 250k reqs * 200 tokens = 50M tokens
- Ingestion/QA: 60k reqs * 1,000 tokens = 60M tokens
- Eligibility: 800k reqs * 40 tokens = 32M tokens
Total ≈ 142M tokens / month (steady-state)

Unit economics (illustrative):
- Redwood inference cost assumption (server-side, optimized, caching/batching): ~$20 / 1M tokens
- Target list price for good gross margin: $50 / 1M tokens -> gross margin ~60% ( (50-20)/50 )
- If you wanted to land in your internal benchmark of $40–$80 / 1M tokens, that mapsto gross margins of ~50%–75% depending on the band.

$/feature example (steady-state average):
- Summary per request: 200 tokens -> 0.2 * $50/1M tokens = $0.01 per summary (note: math is $50/1,000,000 * 200 = $0.01)
- Ingestion QA per request: 1,000 tokens -> $0.05 per request
- Eligibility suggestion per request: 40 tokens -> $0.002 per request

Monthly cost (list price) on 142M tokens @ $50/1M = $7,100 / month (list) — note: that number assumes no further per-request overhead and uses simple token-only model; your expected spend ranges earlier indicate you anticipate $25k–$60k monthly because you include additional usage patterns and retention/reprompting. We’ll reconcile that in the worksheet ribbon.

CAC/payback and margin targets: 
- Typical target: CAC payback 6–9 months for mid-market procurement-led deals.
- If your LTV (license + upsells) expects a 3x gross margin multiple, you’d want gross margin >=50% at list pricing to meet internal profitability targets.
- Suggested commercial approach: start pilot at a slightly higher list price with a consumption discount band for committed monthly tokens (e.g., 10% discount at 0.5–1M/month, 20% at 1–5M/month, etc.) which preserves margin while giving procurement predictability.

Action items:
1) I’m attaching the worksheet (Redwood-Unit-Econ-Worksheet.xlsx) with a sheet that reconciles to your $25k–$60k monthly budget ranges — please review the assumptions column (A).
2) I’ll prepare a 30/60/90 pilot proposal for your procurement template and include the SOC2 evidence link and expected latency targets for eligibility suggestion.

If the $50 / 1M tokens price point looks reasonable as our starting list, I’ll ask pricing to firm up the banded discount table and draft the pilot SOW.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Unit economics deep-dive — FintechX (internal)

Aditya / Laura — forwarding Samir’s confirmation and my proposed unit-econ framing. Key asks from FintechX: 142M steady-state tokens/month (estimate), procurement window in 6–8 weeks, target internal benchmark $40–$80 / 1M tokens, and sub-100ms latency for eligibility.

Recommendation for commercial team:
- Use $50 / 1M tokens as starting list price for the pilot SOW (gives ~60% gross margin vs our $20 cost assumption).
- Offer conditional consumption discounts tied to committed tokens: 10% @ 0.5–1M/month, 15% @ 1–3M, 25% @ >3M.
- Include a latency-based SLA carveout for eligibility (if >150ms, step-down credit applies) — they want sub-100ms, but pilot may tolerate 100–150ms.

Questions for you:
1) Approve starting list price of $50/1M tokens for pricing to formalize (yes/no)?
2) Are the proposed discount bands reasonable from a margin perspective?
3) Any redlines we should avoid before procurement (e.g., long-term minimums, harsh SLA credits)?

I attached the worksheet and proposed pricing grid. If you’re good, I’ll have pricing draft the formal bands and I’ll send FintechX a pilot SOW draft this week.
